paperName: The National Economy in a Global Context

questions.questionText: An economy experiences a positive supply-side shock. Other things remaining equal, the impact on the economy is most likely to be

options.text: higher inflation and faster economic growth.
higher output and lower inflation.
lower employment and slower economic growth.
lower unemployment and a larger budget deficit.

questions.questionText: The quantity of food imported by an economy increases by 12% in one year. The most likely cause is a fall in

options.text: domestic farm prices.
income tax.
the exchange rate.
welfare benefits.

questions.questionText: Figure 1 shows aggregate demand (AD) curves for an economy. Which one of the following is most likely to cause the aggregate demand curve to shift from AD1 to AD2?

options.text: A fall in imports
A fall in the price level
A reduction in the budget deficit
A rise in the exchange rate

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements about the consumer price index (CPI) is correct?

options.text: A fall in the CPI means that the real value of money is falling
An increase in the CPI means that the rate of inflation is rising
The CPI measures changes in the prices of goods and services bought by households
The weights used in the CPI reflect changes in the quality of goods and services

questions.questionText: An economy has recently recovered from a recession and closed its negative output gap. The government would now like to increase the trend rate of economic growth. Which one of the following policies is likely to be the most effective?

options.text: Expansionary fiscal policy
Expansionary monetary policy
Redistributive policies
Supply-side policies

questions.questionText: The government invests £1 billion in an extension to the motorway network. As a result, in addition to this initial investment, national income increases by a further £2 billion. What is the value of the multiplier?

An economy is experiencing short-run economic growth accompanied by falling unemployment. This is due to rising aggregate demand following the introduction of an expansionary fiscal policy. Which one of the following is most likely to help the economy avoid rising inflation?

options.text: A fall in the exchange rate and falling productivity
A fall in the exchange rate and rising productivity
A rise in the exchange rate and falling productivity
A rise in the exchange rate and rising productivity

questions.questionText: Figure 2 shows the aggregate demand (AD) curves and short-run aggregate supply (SRAS) curves for an economy. Which one of the following combinations of events is most likely to cause aggregate demand to shift from AD1 to AD2 and short-run aggregate supply from SRAS1 to SRAS2?

options.text: A fall in income tax and lower raw material prices
A fall in net exports and higher labour productivity
A rise in money wages and a rise in household saving
An increase in VAT and a rise in household wealth

questions.questionText: A government wishes to reduce the surplus on the current account of the balance of payments. Which one of the following sets of policies is likely to be the most successful?

questions.questionText: In which one of the following situations is there most likely to be cyclical unemployment in an economy?

options.text: Absence of an output gap
Generous unemployment benefits
Many firms with excess capacity
Widespread investment in labour-saving equipment

questions.questionText: At the start of the year, the national debt for an economy was £920 billion. In the previous year, the budget deficit was £60 billion. In the current year, government spending is projected to fall by £20 billion and tax revenues to increase by £10 billion from last year’s levels. Other things remaining equal, the expected size of the national debt at the end of the current year is

options.text: £890 billion.
£950 billion.
£960 billion.
£980 billion.

questions.questionText: Figure 3 shows an economy’s aggregate demand (AD) and short-run aggregate supply (SRAS) curves. The initial equilibrium price level is at OP1. Which one of the following is most likely to be responsible for both the cost–push and demand-pull inflationary pressures that raise the price level to OP2?

options.text: A fall in interest rates
A fall in the exchange rate
A rise in direct taxes
A rise in indirect taxes

questions.questionText: Other things remaining the same, the current account deficit of an economy’s balance of payments is most likely to

options.text: become smaller as domestic inflation falls below foreign inflation rates.
deteriorate when there is an upturn in economic activity overseas.
improve when there is a rise in the exchange rate.
increase when there is an improvement in the economy’s international competitiveness.

questions.questionText: Which statement applies to progressive taxes, but does not apply to proportional or regressive taxes? As income falls

options.text: a larger percentage of income is taken in tax.
a smaller percentage of income is taken in tax.
less income is taken in tax.
the same percentage of income is taken in tax.

questions.questionText: Figure 4 shows the performance of an economy through time. As the economy moves from point A to point B, it can be concluded that

options.text: the economy has completed one economic cycle.
the level of GDP per head has risen.
the rate of economic growth has increased.
the trend rate of growth is higher.

questions.questionText: Output of the UK economy is at the normal capacity level and the Bank of England decides to implement measures to restrict the supply of credit to households. The most likely reason for this policy is that

options.text: earnings are increasing fast.
house prices are falling.
productivity is growing more quickly.
the exchange rate is appreciating.

questions.questionText: Table 1 shows the index of export prices, the current monetary value of a country’s exports and the calculated value, to the nearest £ billion, of the value of its exports at 2017 prices. Which one of the following is correct?

options.text: The value of the country’s exports in 2016 at 2017 prices, to the nearest £ billion, was £162 billion
The value of the country’s exports in 2016 at 2017 prices, to the nearest £ billion, was £198 billion
The value of the country’s exports in 2019 at 2017 prices, to the nearest £ billion, was £240 billion
The value of the country’s exports in 2019 at 2017 prices, to the nearest £ billion, was £250 billion

options.text: A lower rate of corporation tax
A reduction in the money supply
An increase in state pensions
An increase in the exchange rate

questions.questionText: If the current account of the balance of payments is in surplus, then

options.text: the exchange rate of the country’s currency must be appreciating.
the net value of trade in goods and services plus the net value of primary and secondary income must be positive.
the total of all money flows into the economy must be greater than the total of all money flows out.
the value of exports of goods and services must be greater than the value of imports of goods and services.

questions.questionText: The level of unemployment in an economy has fallen. The most likely cause is

options.text: a reduction in firms’ profits.
a rise in the retirement age.
an increase in immigration.
lower mortgage interest rates.
